title: Count Cold Days
description: A weather station recorded n daily temperatures. Read an integer threshold and the n readings, then count how many days were strictly colder than the threshold, using a loop and an accumulator. A reading t counts only when t < threshold; a reading exactly equal to the threshold does not count. This is the transfer variant of 'Count Divisible Numbers': same loop-bounds and accumulator skill, different surface story and filter predicate.
constraints: Each of the n temperatures satisfies -100 <= value <= 100
starter_code:
def count_cold_days(temps, threshold):
    """Return how many temperatures in temps are strictly below threshold."""
    # TODO: implement using a loop and an accumulator
    raise NotImplementedError


def main():
    import sys
    data = sys.stdin.read().strip().split()
    if not data:
        return
    n = int(data[0])
    threshold = int(data[1])
    temps = list(map(int, data[2:2 + n]))
    print(count_cold_days(temps, threshold))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
input_format: First line: two integers n and threshold separated by a space. Second line: n integers (the daily temperatures) separated by spaces.
output_format: A single integer: how many of the n temperatures are strictly below threshold.
